edges.description: Attached to the telomere/senescence node rather than to the downstream tissue-exhaustion node, because the route to malignancy is the genomic instability of critically short telomeres — chromosome-end fusion and breakage-fusion-bridge cycles — not the loss of stem-cell output itself. The two consequences of short telomeres diverge here: exhaustion produces the marrow failure, instability produces the clonal evolution.
edges.source: Critically Short Telomeres and Replicative Senescence

edges.description: The solid-tumour arm of the same genomic instability, arising characteristically in the head and neck and anogenital epithelia — the same high-turnover mucosal surfaces that carry the leukoplakia.
edges.source: Critically Short Telomeres and Replicative Senescence

edges.description: A feature of the severe end of the spectrum rather than of classic DC: Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome is the variant defined by the shortest telomeres and earliest onset. Linked from this node rather than from tissue exhaustion because it is developmental — the cerebellum is not a high-turnover tissue — and the mechanism by which telomere shortening produces it is not established.
edges.source: Critically Short Telomeres and Replicative Senescence

edges.description: The other severe-variant feature, defining Revesz syndrome, which dismech curates as its own entry. Same reasoning as the cerebellar feature: linked from the telomere node, with the mechanism unestablished.
edges.source: Critically Short Telomeres and Replicative Senescence

edges.description: The nail bed is one of the high-turnover epithelia this node names, so nail dystrophy is the same exhaustion expressed in a different tissue as the marrow failure. It is the first component of the classic mucocutaneous triad.

edges.description: The second component of the triad. Skin is a continuously renewing epithelium, and the lacy pigmentation of the upper chest and neck is the cutaneous form of the same stem-cell exhaustion.

edges.description: The third component, in the oral mucosa — another high-turnover epithelium. It also matters beyond the triad, being the tissue from which the head-and-neck squamous carcinomas of this disease arise.
edges.source: Stem Cell Exhaustion in High-Turnover Tissues

edges.description: Lymphocytes are among the most proliferative cells in the body, so the telomere reserve is exhausted there as it is in the marrow. The immunodeficiency of DC is therefore part of the same high-turnover failure rather than a separate lesion.

edges.description: The knock-in reproduces the upstream lesion of this entry: telomerase activity at telomeres falls in the presence of the mutant protein and telomeres shorten with successive generations.
edges.limitations: The generational phenotype requires homozygosity, whereas human PFBMFT8 carriers are heterozygous; heterozygous mice show only a trend toward shorter telomeres. Mouse telomeres are far longer than human telomeres, which is why several generations of intercross are needed before a phenotype appears at all.

edges.description: Old knock-in mice develop profibrotic lung pathology - alveolar septal thickening, inflammatory infiltrate and increased alpha-smooth muscle actin - but this stops short of the established fibrosis that defines the human phenotype.
edges.limitations: Masson trichrome staining found no significant difference in lung collagen between knock-in and wild-type animals; only a single G3 homozygote reached extensive collagen deposition. So the model reproduces a profibrotic tendency, not idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and it does so only in homozygotes at old age.

nodes.description: Defective maintenance leads to progressive telomere attrition until telomeres become critically short or dysfunctional. Critically short telomeres are sensed as DNA damage, activating the p53/p21 DNA damage response and driving affected cells into replicative senescence or apoptosis, thereby limiting the replicative capacity of the tissue. Very short telomeres (often below the 1st percentile for age) are the diagnostic hallmark of DC.

nodes.description: The unifying upstream defect in DC is impaired telomere maintenance. Germline pathogenic variants in genes encoding telomerase (TERT catalytic subunit, TERC RNA template), the H/ACA snoRNP that stabilizes TERC (DKC1/dyskerin, NHP2, NOP10, NAF1), telomerase trafficking factors (WRAP53/TCAB1), the shelterin complex (TINF2, ACD/TPP1, POT1), the CST replication complex (CTC1, STN1, RPA1), and the RTEL1 helicase reduce the cell's ability to replenish telomeric repeats. Telomeres are nucleoprotein caps that prevent activation of the DNA damage response at chromosome ends.

nodes.description: Because telomere reserve restricts replicative capacity, tissues with high proliferative demand are preferentially affected. Premature replicative exhaustion of stem and progenitor cells in the bone marrow, immune system, skin and mucosa, liver, and lung produces the characteristic multisystem phenotype: bone marrow failure, mucocutaneous changes, and hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis. Genomic instability from dysfunctional telomeres also underlies the predisposition to myelodysplastic syndrome, leukemia, and squamous cell carcinoma.
